RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday, November 19, 2010/Kartika 28, 1932 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs, Food
and Public Distribution; Human Resource Development; Micro, Small and
Medium Enterprises; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions — 20
44
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Opposition to semester
system
*141. SHRI SHYAMAL
CHAKRABORTY: Will the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Delhi
University has introduced semester system
in 13 under-graduate science courses;
(b) whether it is also a fact that Delhi
University Teachers’ Association (DUTA)
is protesting against the semester system;
and
(c) if so, what amicable settlement the
Ministry is making to reign in DUTA on
semester system?
Commercialisation of education
†*142. SHRI RAGHUNANDAN
SHARMA: Will the Minister of
HUMANRESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that
commercialisation of education is taking
place rapidly;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the steps being taken by
Government to check this
commercialisation?
Impact of floods and drought on
agriculture products
*143. SHRI SATYA VRAT
CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has made any
assessment about the losses suffered by
States and farmers due to the recent floods
in different parts of the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the steps taken by Government to
extend the required financial and other
assistance to the affected States;
(d) whether it is a fact that a large number
of districts were also adversely affected
due to drought during the last kharif season;
and
(e) if so, the details of the districts and
the losses suffered by each district and the
nature of assistance given by the Central
Government?

45
Assistance to displaced persons from
mining areas
*144. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRA-
SEKHAR: Will the Minister of STEEL be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the steel
making companies in the country have been
asked to give 26 per cent profits from
mining for displaced persons of mining
areas;
(b) if so, the details thereof;  and
(c) how this provision is likely to be
implemented?
Criteria for fixing MSP
†*145. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that at the end of
the current year Government proposes to
increase the Minimum Support Prices
(MSP) of agricultural products of rabi
crops to arrive after April, 2011;
(b) if so, the names of the products and
the amount of increase in their value;
and
(c) the reasons for not adopting similar
criteria for increasing Minimum Support
Prices of all the agricultural products?
Implementation of Village Grain
Bank Scheme
*146. SHRI BHAGAT SINGH
KOSHYARI: Will the Minister of
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to
state:
(a) the details regarding the guidelines
issued by Government for implementation
of Village Grain Bank Scheme;
(b) whether the targets fixed for setting
up of Village Grain Banks during the Tenth
Five Year Plan have been achieved;
(c) if so, the details of the targets fixed
and achieved during the said period,
State-wise;
(d) the details of targets fixed by
Government for Eleventh Five Year Plan,
State-wise; and
(e) the steps taken to achieve the said
targets?
Formation of students' unions in
Central Universities
†*147. SHRI MOHAN SINGH: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of Central Universities
as on date;
(b) the universities where students’
unions are in existence and the number of
universities where demand for formation
of students' union is pending;
(c) whether Government is considering
to constitute students’ union as per the
directions of Supreme Court and the
recommendations of Lyngdoh Committee
in all such universities;  and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Allocation of fertilizers to States
†*148. SHRI BALA V ANT ALIAS BAL
APTE: Will the Minister of CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether any concrete steps have
been taken by Government to prevent the
hoarding of fertilizers;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

46
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether, in view of growing demand
for fertilizers with nutrients, Government
has worked on any plan to supply adequate
amount of fertilizers; and
(d) if so, the details of the quantity of
fertilizers allocated to various States so far?
Shifting of DRM office from Kalupur
to Sabarmati
*149. SHRI NATUJI HALAJI
THAKOR: Will the Minister of
RAILWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has issued any
order to the General Manager (G.M.),
Western Railways with regard to shifting
of Divisional Railway Manager (DRM)
office from Kalupur to Sabarmati Railway
Station area;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether budgetary support has been
granted for construction of office building
at Sabarmati;
(d) if so, the details of funds earmarked
for the purpose; and
(e) the time by when the new building
will be constructed?
Irregularities in IIT-JEE
*150. SHRI BALWINDER SINGH
BHUNDER: Will the Minister of
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government’s attention has
been drawn to the write up ‘I.I.T.—Kgp
ignored C.V .C. advice way back in 2006’
which appeared in a prominent daily on 28
October, 2010, about irregularities
committed by the Chairman of I.I.T.—
J.E.E. in 2006;
(b) if so, whether the matter has been
inquired into with particular reference to
the allegations made by C.V .C. in the case
and the shredding of the J.E.E., 2006 papers
in haste to destroy evidence; and
(c) if so,the findings of the inquiry and
the action taken thereon and if not, the
reasons for ignoring the matter so far?
Poor service conditions of teaching
and non-teaching staff of self-
financing colleges
*151. SHRI K.N. BALAGOPAL: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of the
poor service conditions of teaching and non-
teaching staff of self-financing colleges in
the country;
(b) if so, the steps taken by Government
to overcome this problem; and
(c) whether Government would initiate
steps to enact a Model Law to protect the
basic service conditions of the employees
of self-financing colleges?
Norms for coverage under NAIS
*152. SHRI A VTAR SINGH
KARIMPURI: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) the norms laid down for coverage
under the National Agriculture Insurance
Scheme (NAIS);
(b) whether the said norms are being
followed;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) the details of funds released under
the Scheme during each of the last three
years, State-wise, especially for Punjab?

47
Distribution of foodgrains
*153. SHRI R.C. SINGH: Will the
Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the NAC has
created two new Categories, setting aside
BPL criteria for distribution of foodgrains
under the National Food Security Scheme;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the total number of people going to
be benefited from the above
recommendation, State-wise; and
(d) the burden on Government in the
form of subsidy, etc.?
Specially reserved coaches for
disabled passengers
*154. SHRIMATI KANIMOZHI: Will
the Minister of RAILW AYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether reserved coaches for
disabled passengers have been restored;
(b) the trains which currently have the
facility of specially reserved coaches for
the disabled and the details thereof; and
(c) the steps taken by Government to
provide ticket reservation facilities for the
differently-abled persons and the details
thereof?
Allotment of telephone booths to
disabled persons
†*155. SHRI UPENDRA
KUSHWAHA: W ill the Minister of
RAILWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Railways
have allotted STD, PCO booths to disabled
persons at major stations;
(b) whether it is also a fact that
previously, extension in tenure to these
booths was being given for a period of two
years;
(c) whether it is a fact that this time,
extension to these booths has been given
for a period of two months only which will
expire on 31 December, 2010 after which
the young disabled booth operators will be
rendered unemployed; and
(d) if so, whether Government proposes
to provide permanent employment to these
disabled persons?
Essential Commodities Act
†*156. SHRI NARESH CHANDRA
AGRAWAL: W ill the Minister of
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to
state:
(a) when was the Essential
Commodities (EC) Act implemented in the
country and what were the circumstances
at the time of implementation which
necessitated enactment of this law;
(b) whether it is a fact that those
circumstances are not prevailing at present
and as  a result traders are opposing this
black law;
(c) if so, whether Government will
consider to roll back this law; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Production of kharif crops
*157. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether production of kharif crops
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

48
for 2009-10 is estimated at 98.83 million
tonnes which is lower than the target of
125.15 million tonnes set for the year;
(b) if so, the appropriate measures
Government is taking to meet this situation;
and
(c) whether the area coverage under total
foodgrains during kharif 2009-10 compared
to that during kharif 2008-09 shows a
decline of 46.18 lakh hectare(ha)?
Subsidy and cost of fertilizers
*158. SHRI VIJAY JAW AHARLAL
DARDA: Will the Minister of
CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that with the
progressive steep increase in fertilizer
subsidy presently touching the figure of
Rupees one lakh crores, the price
component has eaten up to 94 per cent and
that a mere 6 per cent increase is spent
towards higher consumption in agricultural
operations;
(b) if so, why our cost of fertilizer
production is increasing alarmingly; and
(c) how this escalation compares with
production of fertilizers in countries like
China?
Elephants killed in train  accidents
*159. SHRI JAI PRAKASH
NARAYAN SINGH: Will the Minister of
RAILWAYS be pleased to state:
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 13th November, 2010 Secretary-General.
Kartika 22, 1932 (Saka)
(a) whether it is a fact that some
elephants have been killed due to train
accidents in Kerala and Assam recently;
(b) if so, the details in this regard; and
(c) the steps being taken by
Government to protect the elephants by
erecting fences at important junctions to
avoid such accidents in future?
Guidelines regarding provision of
subsidised grains
*160. SHRI P. RAJEEVE: W ill the
Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has carried out
a fresh survey to ascertain the number of
citizens who are in the categories of Above
the Poverty Line, Below the Poverty Line
and the Antyodaya Anna Yojana;
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor;
(c) whether Government has taken
steps to abolish the Above the Poverty
Line category as recommended by the
Supreme Court or modified the guidelines
regarding provision of subsidised grain to
include only those whose annual income is
below ` 2,00,000 per annum; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?

I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)
Agriculture : 143, 145, 152, 157,
Chemicals and Fertilizers : 148, 158,
Consumer Affairs, Food and Public
Distribution : 146, 153, 156, 160,
Human Resource Development : 141, 142, 147, 150, 151,
Micro, Small and Medium
Enterprises :—
Railways : 149, 154, 155, 159,
Steel : 144.
GMGIPMRND—5116RS(S-3)—13.11.2010
